claim: json_escape handled \\ " \n \t but not \r, so a value carrying a carriage return still emitted an invalid record — the exact failure the fix exists to prevent
the old duplicate-key behaviour was a spoofing path: agent=someone-else was last-wins, so an agent could attribute its own action to another in the ADR 0003 audit record
a naive refusal mid-loop would append half a record and corrupt the log the refusal protects; validation now completes before any byte is printed

json_escape forks a subshell per key and per value where the old code expanded inline — rejected: guard.sh runs a handful of times per agent run, and one function removes the escape logic duplicated across cmd_log and cmd_finding

cmd_stop swallows cmd_log failure with || true, so a bad pair there would report a successful stop having logged nothing — rejected: stopping the fleet must never fail on a logging error, and the stop file is the thing that matters
